{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start of the round: a large body with the nose on the left and a forked tail on the right. That outline reads clearly to a judge who doesn't know our plan. I laid the start domino and built stroke 1, the top line of the body, from the nose along the back and on toward the tail crossing. That line carries the fall for the whole top half of the picture. At the end, the table showed all 111 standing dominoes connected to the start.

Execution: I stayed on stroke 1 and kept laying dominoes in short, steady builds until the top run reached the crossing near the tail neck. I then inspected the area closely to check the chain before the five-minute call. Once the fish was connected, I kept my hands off the crossing so a bump wouldn't break the run.

Collaboration: At the start I suggested a split of work: I would take the top line, Maya the bottom, and Tom and Leo the tail. I backed the team's decision to move the start to the nose so both body lines could be reached by the fall. I confirmed with the group that the pad showed the right start before I traced. Later I agreed with the group to keep hands off, and I offered to fix any gap that someone spotted.

Leadership: I set the direction early by choosing the animal, the layout and the roles, so the table could start building right away. I kept my own part simple and finished it, and I helped the team agree to stop touching a finished chain. I believe my share of the table's result was about 30%, mostly from the concept and the top line.", "my_share_percent": 30}
